idiom_name: class (or object expression) over mutableMapOf implementing the repository interface
implementation_notes: Kotlin makes the fake a one-liner: a class backed by mutableMapOf implements the collaborator interface with working behaviour, and an object expression (object : UserRepository {}) serves when the fake is needed at a single call site - the classic heavyweight double class collapses into an ordinary declaration. MockK and similar libraries generate mocks with expectations, so they serve the mock rows rather than this one. Create the fake per test (or clear the map) and keep a test against the real implementation to catch drift.
pitfalls: mutableMapOf is not thread-safe, and a fake held in a companion object or top-level property is shared by the whole suite - keep it per-test.
An object expression captures its enclosing scope, which can pin a large fixture in memory; switch to a named class once the fake grows.
Kotlin's platform types make it easy to return null from an interface method that the real implementation never returns as null - keep the declared nullability.
